thread:
alex_chiu: incident-bot alerted p99 and streaming stalls for /v1/generate around 18:10 UTC, multiple customers reporting timeouts. I see p95 ~420ms -> 1.2s and p99 ~3.5s.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0314-72. Severity: Sev2. Pager notified: @sre_pete.

maria_ng: seeing spike correlating with increased paging on cache-shard-7. Cache hitrate dropped from ~94% to ~28% around 18:09.

devon_r: paging spikes -> CPU saturation on nodes handling streaming sessions, KV cache miss amplification. traces show many requests falling back to full KV loads.

sre_pete: copying relevant dashboards: p95/p99 runbook says start mitigation steps A->C. I'm jumping in. Can someone confirm if prefix-hash rollout happened?

alex_chiu: @maria_ng did the prefix-hash deploy go out in the last deploy window? I recall a small change to prefix hashing for multi-tenant prefixes.

maria_ng: yes, we rolled prefix-hash v3 at 17:50 UTC to all regions. Canary looked fine. But hit-rate telemetry for hot prefixes wasn't in canary.

customer_ops: Customer reported increased error rates for streaming sessions (partial responses, stalls). Trying to map to customer impact list now. Might be 3 enterprise customers affected.

ingrid_k: adding quick timeline: 17:50 prefix-hash v3 rollout -> steady for 15m -> 18:09 hit-rate collapse -> p95 climb -> 18:12 alerts.

sre_pete: immediate mitigation plan: 1) push routing to cache-fallback-variant that bypasses prefix grouping (fast fallback), 2) toggle cache warmup for top prefixes, 3) roll back prefix-hash v3 if needed. We'll do A then B then C.

devon_r: recommend enabling `streaming-small-buffer` mode to reduce tail memory pressure. Command: `./opsctl feature-set --set streaming-small-buffer=true --scope prod`

alex_chiu: I'm going to reroute 20% of traffic to shard-group-b (less loaded) as a quick capacity relief. Doing gradual 5% steps.

oncall-bot: Routing policy update in progress: shard-group-b ramp 5% -> 10% -> 20%.

maria_ng: starting cache invalidation for suspect prefix bucket to force repopulation: `redis-cli -h cache-prod-7 keys "pref:tenant:*" | xargs -n 100 redis-cli -h cache-prod-7 del` (running carefully).

customer_ops: ETA to notify affected customers? We should surface mitigation steps and expected time to full recovery (~30-60m?).

sre_pete: I'll draft a short status: "We are investigating increased latency and streaming stalls affecting a subset of customers. Mitigations in progress: traffic reroute, cache warmup, and a possible rollback of a prefix hashing change. No data loss. Updates every 15 minutes."

ingrid_k: monitoring: p95 dropped to ~350ms after 15% reroute, p99 still ~1.6s but trending down. Cache hit-rate for hot keys rising to ~62% after invalidation and warmup.

devon_r: enabling stream-small-buffer now. Also starting a background warmup job to prefetch top 500 prefixes for affected tenants: `python tools/prefetch_top_prefixes.py --tenants 3 --top 500`

alex_chiu: any sign we need a rollback? If p99 doesn't recover after warmup + reroute, we should prepare rollback of prefix-hash v3. Who owns the rollback? @maria_ng

maria_ng: I'll prepare the rollback playbook. Rolling back requires coordinated config push across regions and a cache tombstone step. Estimate 10m prep.

oncall-bot: Note: new deployment ticket created: DEP-rollback-prefixhash-1897654321. Do not merge other deploys until resolved.

customer_ops: Customer A confirmed improvement in response times after 25m. They report streaming resumed. Marking as partially mitigated.

ingrid_k: p99 at 45 minutes is ~900ms, p95 ~270ms, error rate normalized to baseline. Suggest keeping mitigations for another hour and then assess for rollback.

alex_chiu: agree. Keep rollback staged but hold unless we see regression in next 30m. Also run postmortem sampling for requests that hit cache miss path: `select * from traces where cache_hit=false and route="/v1/generate" limit 200`

maria_ng: started sampling. First 200 traces show majority of misses are for prefixes with altered hash mod 128 -> they now land on different shards with cold caches. That explains low hit rate.

sre_pete: action items: 
- @alex_chiu keep routing at 20% to shard-group-b and monitor
- @maria_ng prep rollback playbook but hold
- @devon_r continue warmup + stream buffer mode
- @ingrid_k continue p99/p95 telemetry and update customer_ops
- @customer_ops notify impacted customers of partial recovery and that a rollback is staged if needed

customer_ops: sending update to customers now.

oncall-bot: Incident severity downgraded to Sev3 at 19:05 UTC (partial mitigation achieved).

alex_chiu: logging timeline for postmortem. We'll include: root cause (prefix-hash mod change), why canary missed it (no hot-prefix telemetry), mitigation steps (reroute, warmup, stream-small-buffer), why rollback was staged but not executed, customer impact, and followups (include pre-canary warmup and canary-level hit-rate checks).

maria_ng: follow-ups: add a canary metric for top-100 prefixes per region, and add an automated warmup job triggered after prefix-hash changes.

sre_pete: thanks everyone. I'll keep the incident open for 2 hours for observation, then transition to post-incident channel. Great coordination. :thumbsup:

alex_chiu: closing chat loop here; will post postmortem draft in ~24h.
